main_text.l: dicta videtur, Inq. Ægypto maximeq;, Ale-xandria peculiarem eius fuisse vsum certissimi. Autores tradunt, vnde non mirandum si elephas morbus in Ægypto fuerit vulgatissimus. Heraclidi Tarentino edulium ex beta lentibus dicebatur [illegible, ~8 letters], quem ci- [?]. Bumtum[?] bene, tum male valentibus exhibebat, constatq; expugnantibus naturis, beta enim mi-nus, lens autem magis subducitur, unde e[?]mentum, quod ex bis in corpus distribuitur, tri-q;, naturam referre necesse est. Panis denig; ex lentibus rarissime aut nunquam confectus invenitur.

Hactenus fuerunt culinaria legumina, se-quuntur medicinalia: (De vicia enim, eruo, [?] similibus hic multum differe, opera pre-tium non est, cum inter pecudum pabula magis enumerentur, quam alimenta hominum, ac non nisi annona e[?]ftuante[?] fame urgente me-

liorum q; penuria in hominum cibatum admit-tantur) quae Medicorum [?] pharma-copolis committimus, in humaniorum enim [?] nitidioris vita hominum mensis nullum ha-benus, [?]tenus obtinuisse locum certum est, quare abdi-canda funt.
Lupinos protogeni pi-ctori comedendos re-linquimus. Cicer fen pi(s)um rubeum raro epipa-rasmen[?]fubit, in medicina autem [?] lupi-num, [?] cicer praeclaros habere vsu comper-tum est.

marginalia.note: Elephan tiafis cur Alexan- drinis pe culiaris

page.notes: Printed page is low contrast and show-through from the reverse is present throughout; several words are doubtful. Greek words in the paragraph beginning "Heraclidi Tarentino" are not legible on the scan and are marked as illegible. The reading of "bumtum", "e[?]mentum", "ἐ/ꝯ" glyphs before "lentibus", "fe-/se-quuntur", "eruo", and the line after "canda" is uncertain. The margin note at the left is printed in several short lines and is given as one note; its exact wording is uncertain. "Semi-" at the lower right is treated as a catchword.
